counterfactual_missing_items: No supplied span explicitly isolates pembrolizumab as the sole trigger, because pemetrexed was co-administered.
No serologic or systemic scleroderma criteria (e.g., ANA, anti-Scl-70, Raynaud's) are provided; the match is clinical-histopathologic.
No vessel-wall damage, fibrinoid necrosis, or leukocytoclastic infiltrate is present to support vasculitis.
decisive_items: The edema appeared 5 days after the patient's 8th cycle of chemotherapy and evolved into sclerotic plaques.
Shows normal-appearing epidermis, thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts, and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration.
Ill-defined erythematoedematous plaques with induration symmetrically distributed on the distal two-thirds of the shins.
response.rationale: R2 best fits the composite: acute edema after cycle 8 evolving to sclerotic plaques, symmetric shin distribution, and biopsy showing thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration, the signature of drug-induced scleroderma/morphea-like reaction. R1 is overly broad and anchored only to drug exposure; R5 conflicts with the histology and the afebrile, non-inflamed profile, which point away from vasculitis.

rejected.why: Histopathology shows thickened collagen and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration rather than vessel-wall vasculitis; afebrile status and normal inflammatory markers further disfavor cutaneous vasculitis.
